rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The likeness is a description for the people of Mecca; mathal means a likeness.
rows.anchor: يعني وصف لهم، يعني لأهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two brothers were Israelites: the believer was Yamlīkha, the unbeliever Firtas, and each inherited four thousand dinars from their father.
rows.anchor: أحدهما مؤمن واسمه يمليخا، والآخر كافر، واسمه فرطس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer spent his inheritance on the poor, orphans, and needy; the unbeliever invested in houses, livestock, and gardens.
rows.anchor: فعمد المؤمن فأنفق ماله على الفقراء واليتامى والمساكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelieving brother is the one given two gardens.
rows.anchor: يعني الكافر، { جنتين من أعناب وحففناهما بنخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each garden yielded all its fruit without reduction; “wronging” the fruit means diminishing it, as in 2:57.
rows.anchor: يعني ولم تنقص من الثمر شيئا، يعني جمله وافرا، نظيرها في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A river was made to run through the middle of the two gardens.
rows.anchor: يعني أجرينا النهر وسط الجنتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbeliever's thamar was wealth in gold, silver, and other kinds of property.
rows.anchor: وكان للكافر مال من الذهب والفضة، وغيرها من أصناف الأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After becoming poor, the believer came to his brother seeking generosity; the account contrasts his worn state with the unbeliever's fine clothes and mount.
rows.anchor: فلما افتقر المؤمن، أتى أخاه الكافر متعرضا لمعروفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer says he lent his inheritance to God, the faithful and enduring, for himself and his children; the unbeliever mocks this belief as waste.
rows.anchor: أقرضته إلهي الملي الوفي، فقدمته لنفسي ولولدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion is the believing brother, and يحاوره means answering or conversing back and forth.
rows.anchor: { وهو يحاوره } ، يعني يراجعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbeliever's boast of greater wealth and standing includes having more children.
rows.anchor: يعني وأكثر ولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden is his orchard; أظن means suppose, and تبيد means perish.
rows.anchor: وهو بستانه، { وهو ظالم لنفسه قال مآ أظن } ، يعني ما أحسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He thought his garden would never perish.
rows.anchor: أن تبيد } ، يعني أن تهلك، { هذه } الجنة { أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbeliever denied that the Resurrection would occur.
rows.anchor: يعني القيامة كائنة كما تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He claimed that if returned to God in the afterlife he would find a better destination than his garden; munqalab means return.
rows.anchor: في الآخرة، { لأجدن خيرا منها } ، يعني أفضل منها، من جنتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer rebukes his companion for disbelief in the Creator who made him from earth, meaning Adam, then from a drop and fashioned him as a man.
rows.anchor: يعني آدم، عليه السلام؛ لأن أول خلقه التراب، ثم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are moved from their places, leaving the earth exposed of mountains, buildings, trees, and other things.
rows.anchor: من الجبال والبناء والشجر وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone is gathered; nobody is left behind.
rows.anchor: فلم يبق منهم أحد إلا حشرناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣaffan means all together, as in 20:64.
rows.anchor: يعني جميعا، نظيرها في طه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People come individually, without worldly possessions, as when first born with nothing.
rows.anchor: فرادى ليس معكم من دنياكم شىء، { كما خلقناكم أول مرة } ، حين ولدوا وليس لهم شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They had claimed in worldly life that no appointment for resurrection would be made.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا، { أن لن نجعل لكم موعدا } [آية: 48]، يعني ميقاتا في الآخرة تبعثون فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book records their worldly deeds, and criminals fear its account of their sins.
rows.anchor: بما كانوا عملوا في الدنيا بأيديهم، { فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه } ، من المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record counts every small and great sin; all their deeds are present, and God wrongs no one in recompense.
rows.anchor: يعني إلا أحصى الكتاب السيئات، { ووجدوا ما عملوا } ، يعني تعجل له عمله كله، { حاضرا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil describes Iblis as a living being among the angels, a group called jinn.
rows.anchor: وهو حي من الملائكة، يقال لهم: الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis disobeyed his Lord out of pride when ordered to prostrate to Adam.
rows.anchor: يعني فعصى تكبرا عن أمر ربه حين أمره بالسجود لآدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis's progeny are the devils; taking them as awliya means treating them as gods, despite their enmity to Adam's descendants.
rows.anchor: يعني إبليس والشياطين لكم معشر بني آدم عدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheists make a vile exchange by worshipping Iblis instead of God.
rows.anchor: يقول: بئس ما استبدلوا بعبادة الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not make Iblis and his progeny witnesses to the creation of the heavens, earth, or themselves.
rows.anchor: يعني ما أحضرتهم، { خلق السماوات والأرض ولا خلق أنفسهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The misleaders led Adam's descendants astray; ʿaḍud means support and help, which God did not take from them.
rows.anchor: الذين أضلوا بني آدم وذريته، { عضدا } ، يعني عزا وعونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells the polytheists to call the partners they claimed were gods; they cannot answer that they are gods.
rows.anchor: يقول: فسألوهم، فلم يجيبوهم بأنها آلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barrier between the polytheists and their alleged partners is a deep valley in Hell.
rows.anchor: يعني واديا عميقا في جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals know that they will enter the Fire; ظنوا can mean they knew, as in 9:118.
rows.anchor: يعني فعلموا أنهم مواقعوها، يعني داخلوها، نظيرها في براءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No alleged deity can turn the Fire away from them.
rows.anchor: ولم يقدر أحد من الآلهة أن يصرف النار عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣarrafnā means varied or described: the Qur'an presents likenesses about diverse matters.
rows.anchor: يعني لونا، يعني وصفنا، { في هذا القرآن للناس من كل مثل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings are especially prone to argument.
rows.anchor: من كل شبه في أمور شتى، { وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those prevented from belief and seeking forgiveness are the mockers and provisioners at Badr; guidance means the Qur'an and its clarification.
rows.anchor: يعني المستهزئين والمطعمين في غزاة بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The precedent of earlier peoples is worldly punishment; at Badr these people faced killing, angels striking their faces and backs, and their souls being sent to the Fire.
rows.anchor: يعني أن ينزل بهم مثل عذاب الأمم الخالية في الدنيا، فنزل ذلك بهم في الدنيا ببدر من القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative is punishment arriving openly and visibly.
rows.anchor: { أو يأتيهم العذاب قبلا } [آية: 55]، يعني عيانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers bring news of Paradise and warnings of Hell; Meccans objected that God would send a human messenger, as in 17:94.
rows.anchor: بالجنة، { ومنذرين } من النار؛ لقول كفار مكة للنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccan unbelievers argued falsely that messengers were merely humans like them, to invalidate the truth.
rows.anchor: وجدالهم بالباطل قولهم للرسل: ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا، وما أنتم برسل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yudḥiḍū means invalidate the truth brought by messengers, as in 40:5.
rows.anchor: يعني ليبطلوا بقولهم الحق الذي جاءت به الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mocked the Qur'an's signs and warnings, claiming the Qur'an and threatened punishment were nothing from God.
rows.anchor: يعني آيات القرآن وما أنذروا فيه من الوعيد استهزاء منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most unjust are among the Meccan provisioners and mockers, admonished by the Qur'an but refusing to believe.
rows.anchor: نزلت في المطعمين والمستهزئين، فأعرض عن الإيمان بآيات الله القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting what one's hands sent ahead means abandoning past sins without seeking forgiveness for shirk.
rows.anchor: يعني ترك ما سلف من ذنوبه، فلم يستغفر منها من الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coverings prevent understanding the Qur'an and the heaviness in ears prevents hearing it; Meccan unbelievers therefore will not accept guidance.
rows.anchor: يعني القرآن، { وفي آذانهم وقرا }؛ لئلا يسمعوا القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's forgiveness and mercy appear in delaying punishment rather than hastening retribution; otherwise their sins would bring immediate worldly punishment.
rows.anchor: ذو الرحمة } يعني ذا النعمة حين لا يعجل بالعقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment instead has an appointed time, with no refuge from it.
rows.anchor: يعني ميقاتا يعذبون فيه، { لن يجدوا من دونه موئلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The towns were destroyed in worldly punishment for wrongdoing, meaning associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: بالعذاب في الدنيا، يعني أشركوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their destruction was appointed; likewise, the Meccans' destruction was timed for Badr.
rows.anchor: يعني ميقاتا، وهكذا وقت هلاك كفار مكة ببدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses's young companion was Joshua son of Nun, his nephew, from the tribe of Joseph son of Jacob.
rows.anchor: يوشع بن نون، وهو ابن أخت موسى، من سبط يوسف بن يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says he will continue seeking al-Khiḍr, whom Muqatil says descended from ʿAmil among the Israelites.
rows.anchor: يعني لا أزال أطلب الخضر، وهو من ولد عاميل، من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two seas were called al-Rash and al-Karr; they join into one river and flow into the sea beyond Azerbaijan.
rows.anchor: يقال لأحدهما: الرش، وللآخر: الكر، فيجتمعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥuqb means a long period; it is also said to mean eighty years.
rows.anchor: يعني دهرا، ويقال: الحقب ثمانون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Moses claimed no one was more learned, God revealed a more learned servant, al-Khiḍr; Gabriel told Moses to carry a salted fish and seek him where it was forgotten.
rows.anchor: فأوحى الله عز وجل إليه: أن رجلا من عبادي يسكن جزائر البحر، يقال له: الخضر، هو أعلم منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and Joshua carried bread and a salted fish, rested at a rock in Marwan by the Sea of Aylah near the Spring of Life, and the spring revived the fish while Moses slept.
rows.anchor: والصخرة بأرض تسمى: مروان، على ساحل بحر أيلة، وعندها عين تسمى: عين الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fish fell into the sea and swam through water that split around it, leaving a tunnel-like trace.
rows.anchor: فأصابها الماء فعاشت، ونام موسى، فوقعت السمكة في البحر، فجعل لا يمس صفحتها شىء من الماء إلا انفلق عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fish's path was a tunnel, like the mouth of a waterskin.
rows.anchor: يعني الحوت اتخذ سبيله، يعني طريقه في البحر سربا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next morning Joshua forgot to tell Moses about the fish until they had gone farther and become hungry.
rows.anchor: نسي يوشع بن نون أن يخبر موسى، عليه السلام، بالحوت حتى أصبحا وجاعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naṣab means bodily hardship; the source compares it with 38:41.
rows.anchor: يعني مشقة في أبداننا، مثل قوله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awa means they reached the rock; Joshua forgot to tell Moses about the fish.
rows.anchor: يعني انتهينا إلى الصخرة، وهي في الماء، { فإني نسيت الحوت }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source assigns “it took its way” to Moses and says Moses was astonished by the fish's route through the sea.
rows.anchor: يعني موسى، عليه السلام، طريقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They retraced their steps; qaṣaṣan means following a track, as in 28:11.
rows.anchor: يقول: فرجعا يقصان آثارهما، كقوله سبحانه في القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and Joshua followed the fish's route through the sea until they met al-Khiḍr on an island.
rows.anchor: في البحر في أثر الحوت، حتى لقيا الخضر، عليه السلام، في جزيرة في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They found al-Khiḍr praying; God's mercy means prophethood, and the knowledge was granted by God.
rows.anchor: قائما يصلي، { آتيناه رحمة من عندنا } ، يقول: أعطيناه النعمة، وهي النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil says al-Khiḍr was named al-Yasa because his knowledge encompassed six heavens and six earths.
rows.anchor: وإنما سمى اليسع؛ لأن علمه وسع ست سموات وست أرضين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khiḍr wore wool, recognized Moses as Israel's prophet, and said God had made him know Moses.
rows.anchor: فقال: وعليك السلام يا نبي إسرائيل، فقال موسى: وما يدريك أني نبي بني إسرائيل؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks to follow al-Khiḍr and learn; rushd here means knowledge.
rows.anchor: يعني علما

rows.speaker: الخضر
rows.claim: Al-Khiḍr says the Torah gives sufficient knowledge and Moses already has the Israelites to occupy him; Moses repeats his request.
rows.anchor: كفى بالتوراة علما، وببنى إسرائيل شغلا، فأعاد موسى الكلام

rows.speaker: الخضر
rows.claim: Al-Khiḍr predicts Moses cannot be patient because he will do unfamiliar things that Moses will see as marvels and question; khubr means knowledge.
rows.anchor: أعمالا لا تعرفها، ولا تصبر على ما ترى من العجائب حتى تسألني عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses promises patience if God wills and not to disobey al-Khiḍr's instructions or prohibitions; Muqatil says Moses did not remain patient but did not sin by making this conditional promise.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: فلم يصبر مولى، ولم يأثم بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khiḍr asks a passing boat to carry them over the Sea of Aylah; some call them thieves, but the owner sees prophetic faces and takes them for a fare.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب السفينة: أرى وجوه أنبياء، وما هم بلصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khiḍr makes a hole with an adze; water enters, but Moses stuffs clothes into it to stop the leak.
rows.anchor: فعمد الخضر فضرب ناحية السفينة بقدوم فخرقها، فدخل الماء فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses condemns injustice and grabs al-Khiḍr's beard; al-Khiḍr embraces him, recalls their compact, pleads by God, and sits on the hole to keep out water.
rows.anchor: وكان موسى، عليه السلام، ينكر الظلم، فقام موسى إلى الخضر، عليهما السلام، فأخذ بلحيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imran means a reprehensible deed.
rows.anchor: يعني لقد أتيت أمرا منكرا

rows.speaker: الخضر
rows.claim: Al-Khiḍr repeats that Moses would not be patient; Joshua prompts Moses to remember his promise.
rows.anchor: على ما ترى من العجائب، قال يوشع لموسى: اذكر العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turhiq means overwhelm or cover; Moses asks not to be burdened with harshness in what he says.
rows.anchor: يعني تغشيني، { من أمري عسرا } [آية: 73]، يعني من قولي عسرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses privately regrets following al-Khiḍr, thinking he could instead teach God's Book to Israel morning and evening; al-Khiḍr knows this thought.
rows.anchor: ثم قعد موسى مهموما يقول في نفسه: لقد كنت غنيا عن اتباع هذا الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A bird, thought to be a swallow, dips its beak into the sea; al-Khiḍr compares their knowledge of God to that drop compared with the sea.
rows.anchor: يرون أنه خطاف، حتى وقع على ساحل البحر، فنكث بمنقاره في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They leave the boat on the Sea of Aylah and meet a six-year-old boy; al-Khiḍr kills him with a black stone. The boy is Ḥusayn b. Kāzarī, son of Sahuwa.
rows.anchor: غلاما } سداسيا، { فقتله } الخضر بحجر أسود، واسم الغلام: حسين بن كازرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses cannot refrain from condemning the killing, calling the boy pure and without sin deserving death, killed without retaliation.
rows.anchor: يعني لا ذنب لها، ولم يجب عليها القتل، { بغير نفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munkaran means a terrible deed; Joshua tells Moses to recall his promise.
rows.anchor: يقول أتيت أمرا فظيعا، قال يوشع لموسى: اذكر العهد

rows.speaker: الخضر
rows.claim: Al-Khiḍr emphasizes he had already warned Moses about the marvels and his inability to be patient.
rows.anchor: لأنه كان قد تقدم إليه قبل ذلك بقوله

rows.speaker: موسى
rows.claim: After the killing, Moses says that another question may end their companionship and that al-Khiḍr has given him sufficient excuse.
rows.anchor: يعني بعد قتل النفس، { فلا تصاحبني قد بلغت من لدني عذرا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The village was Bajrawan, also said to be Antioch; Muqatil quotes Qatada identifying it as the village.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: قال قتادة: هي القرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask for food, but the people refuse to host them, meaning to feed them.
rows.anchor: الطعام، تسمى القرية: باجروان، ويقال: أنطاكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wall was near collapse because its clay had crumbled; al-Khiḍr rebuilt and leveled it.
rows.anchor: كانوا بلوا الطين، { فأقامه } الخضر جديدا فسواه

rows.speaker: موسى
rows.claim: Moses objects that al-Khiḍr repaired a wall for those who refused them food or lodging without taking payment.
rows.anchor: عمدت إلى قوم لا يطعمونا ولم يضيفونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ta'wil means outcome, as in 7:53.
rows.anchor: يعني بعاقبة، { ما لم تستطع عليه صبرا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boat belonged to poor workers at sea; al-Khiḍr damaged it to protect it from a king in front of them who seized every sound boat by force; waraʾahum means ahead, as in 76:27.
rows.anchor: يعني أن أخرقها، { وكان ورآءهم ملك } ، يعني أمامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king was Mibdal b. Julandi al-Azdi; taking the boat would wrong its owners, who were not harmed by its damage.
rows.anchor: واسم الملك: مبدلة بن جلندي الأزدي، { يأخذ كل سفينة } صالحة صحيحة سوية، { غصبا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believing parents' son was an unbelieving highway robber and tale-bearer who relied on their defense; they thought him innocent.
rows.anchor: وكان الغلام كافرا، يقطع الطريق، ويحدث الحديث، ويلجأ إليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil glosses khashina as knew, comparing 4:128 and 4:35; the boy's tyranny means wrongdoing that would overwhelm his parents.
rows.anchor: يعني فعلمنا، كقوله سبحانه

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy b. Kaʿb's reading is fa-khāfa rabbuka, meaning your Lord knew.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي بن كعب: فخاف ربك، يعني فعلم ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God intends a replacement better in righteous action and closer in kindness to the parents; Arabs call a boy ghulam until his beard grows.
rows.anchor: والعرب تسمي الغلام غلاما، ما لم تسو لحيته

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says God replaced the murdered son; had he lived, he would have caused his parents to perish through him.
rows.anchor: إن الله عز وجل أبدلهما غلاما مكان المقتول، ولو عاش المقتول لهلكا في سببه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city was Bajrawan, also said to be Antioch; the father was trustworthy and Muqatil gives the family members' names.
rows.anchor: يعني في قرية تسمى: باجروان، ويقال: هي أنطاكية

rows.speaker: الضحاك ومجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and Mujahid say the treasure was pages containing knowledge; another view says it was money.
rows.anchor: قال: صحفا فيها العلم، ويقال: المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boys' father was righteous in the sense of trustworthy; their father, mother, and the two boys are named in the account.
rows.anchor: يعني ذا أمانة، اسم الأب: كاشح، واسم الأم: دهنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boys would reach maturity at eighteen years.
rows.anchor: والأشد ثمانى عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wanted the orphans to reach maturity and retrieve their treasure as mercy; al-Khiḍr acted by God's command, not his own; ta'wil means outcome, as in 7:35.
rows.anchor: ولكن الله أمرني به، { ذلك تأويل } ، يعني عاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn is Alexander Caesar, called the grasping king; Mount Qaf surrounds the world, and he was named for reaching the two solar horns, east and west.
rows.anchor: يعني الإسكندر قيصر، ويسمى: الملك القابض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account to be recited to the people of Mecca is knowledge.
rows.anchor: يا أهل مكة، { ذكرا } [آية: 83]، يعني علما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave him knowledge of the earth's places and routes; sabab means a route or means which he followed.
rows.anchor: يعني علم أسباب منازل الأرض وطرقها، { فأتبع سببا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spring was hot and black; Ibn Abbas says the sun is hotter when rising than setting.
rows.anchor: يعني حارة سوداء، قال ابن عباس: إذا طلعت الشمس أشد حرا منها إذا غربت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the sun is hotter when rising than when setting.
rows.anchor: إذا طلعت الشمس أشد حرا منها إذا غربت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God conveyed the command to Dhul-Qarnayn through Gabriel and gave him the choice to punish or pardon the people.
rows.anchor: أوحى الله عز وجل إليه، جاءه جبريل، عليه السلام، فخبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn says he will kill wrongdoers, who then return to God for terrible punishment in Hell.
rows.anchor: يعني نقتله، { ثم يرد إلى ربه فيعذبه } في الآخرة بالنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believe in God's oneness and act righteously receive Paradise and an easy promise; only one person believed.
rows.anchor: يعني صدق بتوحيد الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following another route means knowing the earth's places and roads.
rows.anchor: يعني علم منازل الأرض وطرقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people had no sun shelter: they lived in underground passages from the heat and emerged to work after it passed; buildings would not stand there.
rows.anchor: كانوا يستقرون في الأرض في أسراب من شدة الحر، وكانوا في مكان لا يستقر عليهم البناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn reached the sunrise as he had the sunset; God says He fully knew what was with him.
rows.anchor: يعني هكذا بلغ مطلع الشمس كما بلغ مغربها، ثم استأنف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following another route means knowing the earth's places and roads.
rows.anchor: يعني علم منازل الأرض وطرقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two sadd are mountains; the people beyond them scarcely understood speech because no one knew their language.
rows.anchor: يعني بين الجبلين، { وجد من دونهما قوما لا يكادون يفقهون قولا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gog and Magog are brothers descended from Japheth son of Noah; their corruption is killing in the land of Muslims, and kharj means payment.
rows.anchor: وهما أخوان من ولد يافث بن نوح، { مفسدون في الأرض } ، يعني بالفساد القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people offer payment for a barrier, but Dhul-Qarnayn says God's gift is better and asks them for manpower.
rows.anchor: يعني جعلا، { على أن تجعل بيننا وبينهم سدا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qūwah means a number of men, as in 11:52; he will build a barrier they cannot reach.
rows.anchor: يعني بعدد رجال، مثل قوله عز وجل في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He fills the pass between the mountains with iron chunks; ṣadafān means the mountains and a vast valley lies between.
rows.anchor: يعني قطع الحديد، { حتى إذا ساوى بين الصدفين } ، يعني حشى بين الجبلين بالحديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people blow on the iron until it is fire, then pour molten copper over it to fuse and strengthen the barrier.
rows.anchor: قال: أعطوني الصفر المذاب أصبه عليه ليلحمه فيكون أشد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man tells the Prophet he saw the barrier; the Prophet asks for its description and hears it resembled a black-and-red patterned mantle.
rows.anchor: قال رجل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: قد رأيت سد يأجوج ومأجوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They could not climb the barrier; yaẓharūhu means ascend it, as in 43:33, nor could they bore through it.
rows.anchor: يعني فما قدروا، { أن يظهروه } على أن يعلوه من فوقه

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali says each man among them has a thousand sons before dying; they labor daily but fail to open the barrier because they do not say God willing.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب، عليه السلام: أنهم خلف الردم، لا يموت منهم رجل حتى يولد له ألف ذكر

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: In Ali's report, a Muslim among them eventually tells them to say in God's name and, when they return saying God willing, they break through a thin shell and escape.
rows.anchor: فيقول لهم المسلم: نرجع غدا إن شاء الله فنفتحه

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali says they spread over the earth, drink the Euphrates, and the rearguard recalls that water had been there.
rows.anchor: فيطوفون الأرض، ويشربون ماء الفرات، فيجيء آخرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn calls the completed barrier a blessing for Muslims because Gog and Magog cannot reach them; it will fall when God's promise arrives.
rows.anchor: يعني هذا الردم، { رحمة } ، يعني نعمة، { من ربي } ، للمسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dakkaʾ means the barrier falls, and God's promise of its collapse is true.
rows.anchor: وكان وعد ربي حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Gog and Magog emerge, a third of Syria's people flee, a third fight, and a third surrender to them.
rows.anchor: ثلث أهل الشام، ويقاتلهم الثلث، ويستسلم لهم الثلث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: While behind the barrier, Gog and Magog surge over one another but cannot escape.
rows.anchor: يعني يوم فرغ ذو القرنين من الردم، { يموج في بعض } ، يعني من وراء الردم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the trumpet, God gathers everyone for resurrection, leaving no one behind.
rows.anchor: يعني بالجمع، لم يغادر منهم أحد إلى حشره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is displayed to Meccan unbelievers of the Qur'an by removing its covering.
rows.anchor: بالقرآن من أهل مكة، { عرضا } [آية: 100]، يعني بالعرض كشف الغطاء عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A veil of unbelief in the Qur'an covers their eyes so they cannot see its guidance; inability to hear means inability to believe.
rows.anchor: يعني عليها غشاوة الإيمان بالقرآن، لا يبصرون الهدى بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ear's waqr means heaviness, as in 18:57.
rows.anchor: يعني الإيمان بالقرآن سمعا، كقوله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccans think idols taken as protectors instead of God will benefit and intercede for them; Hell is their lodging.
rows.anchor: يعني بالآلهة بأن ذلك نافعهم، وأنها تشفع لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuzulan means lodging.
rows.anchor: يعني منزلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Paradise do not die or seek to move elsewhere.
rows.anchor: لا يموتون، { لا يبغون عنها حولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jews challenge Muhammad for claiming wisdom and complete knowledge but saying he lacks knowledge of the spirit; God says his knowledge is little beside God's.
rows.anchor: وتزعم أنه لا علم لك بالروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jewish challenge cites the statement that the spirit is from God's command.
rows.anchor: وتزعم أن الروح من أمر ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet received knowledge, but it is slight compared with God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: إنك أوتيت علما، وعلمك في علم الله قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea as ink represents God's knowledge; it would run out before God's words, even if another sea were added, since no one can encompass God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: يعني علم ربي جل جلاله، { لنفد البحر قبل أن تنفد كلمات ربي } ، يعني علم ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is human like his audience but receives revelation that their God is one God; hoping to meet the Lord means fearing resurrection.
rows.anchor: يقول: ربكم رب واحد، { فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه } ، يقول: من كان يخشى البعث في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Jundub b. Zuhayr al-Azdi, later al-Amiri, who told the Prophet God is rich and does not accept a deed shared with another.
rows.anchor: نزلت في جندب بن زهير الأزدي، ثم العامري، قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says God is the best partner: if another is associated with Him in a deed, He leaves the entire deed to that partner and accepts only what is sincerely His.
rows.anchor: أنا خير شريك، من أشركني في عمل، جعلت العمل كله لشريكي، ولا أقبل إلا ما كان لي خالصا

rows.speaker: شيبان أبو معاوية التميمي
rows.claim: Shayban says God preserves righteous people through their children, linking the claim to the righteous father in 18:82.
rows.anchor: عن شيبان أبي معاوية التميمي، قال: إن الله عز وجل ليحفظ الصالحين في أبنائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source lists the Cave's name as Bangalous, its village as al-Lus, its city as Ephesus, and the dog as Qitmir, then gives names for the judges, king, and youths.
rows.anchor: اسم الكهف: بانجلوس، واسم القرية: اللوس، واسم المدينة: أفسوس، واسم الكلب: قطمير

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr says every earthly language was sent down by God in the Qur'an and gives Gabriel and Michael's names as Abdullah and Ubaydullah.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: ما في الأرض لغة إلا أنزلها الله في القرآن

rows.speaker: عطاء بن خالد
rows.claim: ʿAta b. Khalid says Jesus will perform pilgrimage after descending with seventy thousand, including the Companions of the Cave, who have not died or yet made pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: قال: يحج عيسى إذا نزل في سبعين ألفا، فيهم أصحاب الكهف
